description: Table 6 is a six-column data table rendered as an image (no axes, no scale bar, no figure panels). The column headers read "Deformation conditions", "AGS of DRXGs_I (μm)", "Volume fraction of DRXGs_I", "AGS of DRXGs_II (μm)", "Volume fraction of DRXGs_II" and "AGS of final microstructure (μm)". Six data rows are given, all at 0.9 strain: two constant conditions — 950 °C, 0.1 s⁻¹ and 950 °C, 0.01 s⁻¹ — and four transiently increasing Z_P conditions — 950 °C, 0.01–0.1 s⁻¹ (0.2 strain) and (0.4 strain), and 1050–950 °C, 0.01 s⁻¹ (0.2 strain) and (0.4 strain). The two constant-condition rows carry dashes in all DRXGs columns and give only the final AGS, 31.07 μm and 52.52 μm. In the transient rows the DRXGs_I AGS rises with ε₁ (36.82 → 42.46 μm at 950 °C; 42.90 → 63.29 μm at 1050–950 °C) while its volume fraction rises (0.07 → 0.34; 0.04 → 0.37) and the DRXGs_II fraction falls (0.91 → 0.64; 0.94 → 0.61); the final AGS follows, 33.77 → 37.12 μm and 53.71 → 58.30 μm. The table therefore demonstrates that a transient increase of Z_P leaves a larger residual fraction and larger AGS of DRXGs_I as ε₁ grows, which enlarges the final microstructure AGS.

observations.observation: Table 6 has six columns: "Deformation conditions", "AGS of DRXGs_I (μm)", "Volume fraction of DRXGs_I", "AGS of DRXGs_II (μm)", "Volume fraction of DRXGs_II", "AGS of final microstructure (μm)".
For the constant conditions only the final-microstructure AGS is tabulated — 31.07 μm at 950 °C, 0.1 s⁻¹ and 52.52 μm at 950 °C, 0.01 s⁻¹ — with "—" in all four DRXGs columns.
At 950 °C, 0.01–0.1 s⁻¹ (0.2 strain): AGS of DRXGs_I = 36.82 μm with volume fraction 0.07; AGS of DRXGs_II = 32.93 μm with volume fraction 0.91; AGS of final microstructure = 33.77 μm.
At 950 °C, 0.01–0.1 s⁻¹ (0.4 strain): AGS of DRXGs_I = 42.46 μm with volume fraction 0.34; AGS of DRXGs_II = 33.73 μm with volume fraction 0.64; AGS of final microstructure = 37.12 μm.
At 1050–950 °C, 0.01 s⁻¹ (0.2 strain): AGS of DRXGs_I = 42.90 μm with volume fraction 0.04; AGS of DRXGs_II = 54.41 μm with volume fraction 0.94; AGS of final microstructure = 53.71 μm.
At 1050–950 °C, 0.01 s⁻¹ (0.4 strain): AGS of DRXGs_I = 63.29 μm with volume fraction 0.37; AGS of DRXGs_II = 55.48 μm with volume fraction 0.61; AGS of final microstructure = 58.30 μm.
Raising ε₁ from 0.2 to 0.4 strain increases the volume fraction of DRXGs_I (0.07 → 0.34 at 950 °C; 0.04 → 0.37 at 1050–950 °C) and decreases that of DRXGs_II (0.91 → 0.64; 0.94 → 0.61).
The AGS of the final microstructure increases with ε₁ in both transient conditions: 33.77 → 37.12 μm (950 °C, 0.01–0.1 s⁻¹) and 53.71 → 58.30 μm (1050–950 °C, 0.01 s⁻¹).
The caption states that Table 6 gives AGS evolutions at 0.9 strain under constant conditions and increasing Z_P.

The citing text states that the DRXGs_I were larger than the DRXGs_II, but the 1050–950 °C rows of Table 6 show the opposite ordering at 0.2 strain (DRXGs_I 42.90 μm vs DRXGs_II 54.41 μm), so the statement applies only to part of the tabulated data.

The citing text states that the AGS of DRXGs_II was almost close to the corresponding results under constant conditions at 0.9 strain, while the AGS of DRXGs_I was much greater, especially when ε₁ was 0.4.

The citing text states that the remaining volume fraction and AGS of DRXGs can rise with increasing ε₁ in Table 6, leading to a larger AGS in the final microstructure after transiently increasing Z_P.

The citing text introduces Table 6 in the context of Figs. 27a and 27b, which show AGS evolutions from the first-stage and second-stage DRX grains, indicating the table summarises the same CA simulation outputs at 0.9 strain.

subfigures.description: Single six-column table (no sub-panels): deformation condition vs AGS of DRXGs_I (μm), volume fraction of DRXGs_I, AGS of DRXGs_II (μm), volume fraction of DRXGs_II and AGS of final microstructure (μm), with six rows for constant and transiently increasing Z_P conditions at 0.9 strain.
